title: 'Loudcasters' on English Buses to Face Fines
paragraphs: Bus passengers in England who play music or videos out loud on their phones could soon face fines of up to £100.

The UK government issued new guidance on October 19, encouraging local authorities to use powers that were announced in August. Under these powers, local authorities can create local rules, known as byelaws, against antisocial behavior on buses. They can then issue fines of up to £100 to people who break those rules. However, any new rules must first be approved by the transport secretary.

The rules can cover a range of antisocial behavior, including playing loud music, littering, vaping and threatening behavior. Importantly, the fines will be issued by specialist safety officers, not by bus drivers.

People who play music or videos out loud on public transport, instead of using headphones, are sometimes called "loudcasters." This habit has become a common source of frustration for many passengers.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that loud audio can quickly spoil a journey. At the same time, Burnham launched a national campaign encouraging train passengers to use headphones, with the slogan "share the carriage, not the noise." Playing music out loud on trains is already an offense, but those rules are enforced by the British Transport Police or the train companies. Heidi Alexander said that the actions of an inconsiderate few spoil journeys for everyone else.

Not everyone thinks the new measures go far enough, however. Sharon Graham, the general secretary of the trade union Unite, described the measures as "well meaning" but "wholly inadequate." According to Graham, the penalties will not solve the problems that transport workers face.

Some politicians have called for even tougher action. Over the past year, both the Conservatives and the Liberal Democrats have pushed for stronger measures against loud music on public transport, and the Liberal Democrats have proposed fines of up to £1,000.
England is not the only place taking action. Singapore has also introduced fines for bus passengers who play music out loud.
